evidence: "We need to find a triangle (three nodes all connected to each other)"; "Check for triangle"; the bitset solution builds "adjacency as bitsets" and tests vertex pairs.
affordance_in_statement: A certificate consists of exactly three distinct materials with the following property: it is impossible to distribute these three materials into two separate containers (one of which may be empty) such that within each container, no two materials are mutually volatile.
removal_suggestion: There is no task-preserving rewording that removes this equivalence: for exactly three vertices and two containers, impossibility of a valid partition is intrinsically equivalent to all three pairs being volatile.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the condition as finding a triangle and uses adjacency bitsets for fast triangle/lexicographic search.

common_affordance: For three materials, a two-container partition with no volatile pair inside a container is exactly a proper 2-coloring; it is impossible precisely when the three materials form a triangle.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It constructs non_neighbors of a candidate vertex instead of neighbors, so it searches the complement relation rather than testing whether the three materials are mutually volatile.

recommended_edit: No single valid edit can defeat all survivors without changing the core task. Changing the number of materials or containers would remove the triangle equivalence, but would alter the problem and conflict with the fixed three-integer output/examples.
